model_summary: Integer weekly counts of teachers/trainees starting 2-week training, skilled workers on 40h and 60h, continuous production hours per food and inventory/backlog; minimise wages (360/540 skilled, 120 trainee, 240 trained) plus weekly delay penalties; exactly 50 trainees finished by week 8, <=3 trainees per teacher, skilled headcount 50.
issue_note: The statement does not say whether all booked food must be delivered by the end of week 8 or whether backlog may remain at the horizon (only charged per week of delay). Also unstated: whether newly trained workers may work overtime/teach, and whether early production can be stored (assumed yes, at no cost).

readings.reading: All backlog cleared by end of week 8 (main)
Backlog allowed to remain at end of week 8, penalised only for weeks within the horizon

type_rationale: Worker/trainee counts are integer, production hours, inventory and backlog are continuous; wages, penalties and balance constraints are all linear.
notes: Relaxing all integer counts gives 219412.5 (main reading). Newly trained workers assumed to work 40h only and not to teach; skilled workers who are idle are still paid 360. Objective includes the fixed 50x360x8 skilled wage.

model_summary: Integer units of each product routed through each eligible A and B machine (flow balance A-stage = B-stage per product); maximise sales minus raw material minus machine operating cost charged pro rata (full-capacity cost / effective hours per hour used); machine hour limits.
issue_note: 'Operating costs at full capacity' can be read as cost proportional to hours used (main) or as a fixed cost paid regardless of use; the values differ slightly in the integer model (identical in the LP relaxation since all machines run at capacity).

readings.reading: Machine cost proportional to hours used (main)
Full-capacity operating cost treated as a fixed cost

type_rationale: Product quantities per machine route are treated as integer units; revenue, raw-material and pro-rata machine costs and hour limits are linear (LP if quantities are continuous).
notes: Integrality uncertain: textbook-style continuous model gives 1146.5665.

model_summary: Integer numbers of trucks from warehouses A and B; minimise freight cost subject to minimum daily amounts of raw materials A, B, C.
type_rationale: Two integer truck counts, linear cost and linear covering constraints.
notes: LP relaxation gives the same value.

model_summary: Continuous hectares of soybean/corn/wheat, integer cows, chickens and external labour days per season; maximise crop, livestock and external-work income subject to land (cows need 1.5 ha), funds, seasonal labour, barn and coop capacities.
type_rationale: Crop areas continuous; cows, chickens and (per the whole-day note) external labour days integer; all constraints and objective linear.
notes: Alternative of also forcing labour days used on the farm to be integer (models/industryor-0047__r2.py) gives 20241.7848 (relative difference <1e-4, so not treated as ambiguous). Relaxed value treats all integers as continuous.

model_summary: Integer number of crew starting in each of the six 4-hour periods (each works two consecutive periods, cyclic); minimise total crew subject to each period's requirement.
type_rationale: Six integer headcount variables with linear cyclic covering constraints.
notes: LP relaxation gives the same value; statement asks for an LP formulation but headcounts are integer.

model_summary: Binary hire decisions for five candidates; minimise total salary subject to budget, at most 4 hires, total skill >= 8, total PM experience >= 8, at most one of G and J.
type_rationale: All variables binary, linear objective and constraints.

model_summary: Binary purchase decision per property; maximise annual income subject to budget and not buying both properties 3 and 4.
type_rationale: Four binary variables, linear knapsack and exclusion constraints.

model_summary: Integer numbers of tables, chairs, bookshelves; maximise unit profit (price minus cost) subject to warehouse space, minimum tables and bookshelves, and total item cap.
type_rationale: Three integer item counts, linear profit and constraints.
notes: LP relaxation gives the same value.

model_summary: Binary method choice per task plus integer workers/groups per method; minimise weekly wages plus 500 setup if task 1 uses mixed groups; hour requirements, worker caps 400/800, exclusion rule, >=20 skilled if task 3 uses method B, skilled <= 60% of laborers.
type_rationale: Binary method choices and integer worker/group counts; method linking and if-then rules via big-M with bounds from the worker caps, all linear.
notes: Group effective hours taken as the sum of members' hours (42+2x36, 5x36, 42+3x36); each worker assigned to one task. LP relaxation of counts gives the same value.

model_summary: Binary hire decisions for five candidates; minimise total salary subject to 2-3 hires, budget, at least one Master's/Doctoral, total experience >= 12, at most one of A and E.
type_rationale: All variables binary, linear objective and constraints.

model_summary: Integer spares 0..5 for each of three components; maximise product of tabulated component reliabilities subject to budget 150 and weight 20.
type_rationale: Integer spare counts; objective is a product of tabulated functions of bounded integers, exactly linearisable by one-hot value selection (or binaries over all value combinations), giving an IP.
notes: Solved by complete enumeration of all 216 combinations, so the optimum is global; spares capped at 5 per component as in the table.

model_summary: Number of servings of five foods; minimise cost subject to minimum protein, carbohydrate and calories.
notes: Main model uses integer servings (items priced per unit); continuous quantities give 48.1633.

model_summary: Number of servings of seven foods; minimise cost subject to minimum protein, carbohydrate and calories.
notes: Main model uses integer servings; continuous quantities give 13.1196.

model_summary: Continuous arc flows bounded by capacities with flow conservation; maximise flow from node 0 to node 8.
issue_note: The Node 8 line ('Goods from Node i (x units) can be finally distributed') conflicts with the capacities into node 8 already given in the other lines; read as arcs 8->i (main, irrelevant to the flow) or as capacities i->8 replacing the earlier ones.

readings.reading: Node-8 line lists arcs out of node 8; capacities into node 8 from the other lines (main)
Node-8 line gives capacities into node 8 (overriding)

model_summary: Integer regular-time (<=40) and overtime production and end-of-quarter inventory per quarter; minimise production and holding cost with on-time demand and initial inventory 10.
notes: LP relaxation gives the same value.
